name: gptoss_pilot
description: GPT-OSS-120B systems on the EnterpriseRAG-Bench pilot (50 questions, 10,000-document slice), each scored alone with the official metrics-based evaluation (default settings: citation stripping and document correction on).

systems.name: 4Minds (Constellations)
systems.description: 4Minds prod, Constellations engine (WebSocket), GPT-OSS-120B served by 4Minds; one file per document
caveats: 4Minds: the document IDs come from the chunk document_title (file name <dsid>_<title>.txt), in chunk score order. The instructions of the official prompt are the persona's behavioral guidelines; 4Minds builds its own context and has no per-request system prompt, temperature or max-token setting.

4Minds ingestion time: setup.json counts only from the restart of the wait (21:36 UTC). The upload started at 21:22 UTC and the chunk count did not change after 21:39 UTC, so the ingestion took about 17 minutes (then 15 minutes of stable wait).

systems.name: GPT-OSS + LangChain
systems.description: LangChain TokenTextSplitter (512 tokens, 10% overlap), text-embedding-3-large, FAISS; 100 chunks to the top 10 full documents; the official answer prompt; GPT-OSS-120B on Amazon Bedrock
caveats: LangChain: a copy of the official vector baseline (index_document_vectors.py and vector_retrieval.py) with LangChain parts in place of Qdrant. The official README says 1,024-token chunks; the code uses 512 tokens with 10% overlap, and we follow the code.

systems.name: GPT-OSS + GraphRAG
systems.leaderboard_name: Microsoft GraphRAG 3.3.0 fast, local search (text-embedding-3-large) + GPT-OSS-120B
systems.description: Microsoft GraphRAG 3.3.0, fast indexing method with default settings (1,200-token chunks, noun-phrase graph, community reports by GPT-OSS-120B), text-embedding-3-large; the local search context (community level 2) in the official answer prompt; GPT-OSS-120B on Amazon Bedrock
systems.short: Microsoft GraphRAG, fast method, local search
caveats: GraphRAG: the context is the output of the official local search context builder (reports, entities, relationships and source text units, at most 12,000 tokens), given as one context in the official answer prompt; GraphRAG's own answer prompt is not used. The document IDs are the documents of the text units in the 'sources' table.

GraphRAG index: the community-report calls use GraphRAG's default call settings, not the Bedrock settings of the answer calls. Bedrock's JSON mode often puts a '{' in front of the reply; the hub repairs it in memory (audit/patches/graphrag-3.3.0-gptoss-json-repair.py). 117 of 16,179 communities (0.72%) have no report because the reply stayed invalid.

GraphRAG latency: the search is single-threaded Python over 5.66 million relationships. With 8 parallel workers the questions wait for each other, so the recorded median latency (about 108 s) is mostly waiting; one search alone took 12 to 15 s.

GraphRAG method: this row is not representative of GraphRAG. The fast method writes no entity descriptions (all 73,507 are empty), so local search compares the question only with entity names and often picks generic phrases. A test on 500 documents (the 74 gold documents plus 426 others, same settings) found 17 of 74 gold documents with the fast method and 52 of 74 with the standard method (LLM entity extraction); see the check_graphrag_fast_goldplus and check_graphrag_standard_goldplus steps in audit/audit.log. The row GPT-OSS + GraphRAG (standard) is a standard build of the same slice.
GraphRAG ingestion: the build stopped once in its last step (the OpenAI account had no credits) and that step ran again from the GraphRAG cache. The time is the sum of the two runs, without the wait.

systems.name: GPT-OSS + GraphRAG (standard)
systems.leaderboard_name: Microsoft GraphRAG 3.3.0 standard, local search (text-embedding-3-large) + GPT-OSS-120B
systems.description: Microsoft GraphRAG 3.3.0, standard indexing method with default settings (1,200-token chunks, LLM entity and relationship extraction, description summaries and community reports by GPT-OSS-120B), text-embedding-3-large; the local search context (community level 2) in the official answer prompt; GPT-OSS-120B on Amazon Bedrock
systems.short: Microsoft GraphRAG, standard method, local search
caveats: GraphRAG (standard): the same answer path as the fast row (the official local search context builder, at most 12,000 tokens, as one context in the official answer prompt; document IDs from the 'sources' table). Only the index is different: 121,944 entities with descriptions and 256,481 relationships.

GraphRAG (standard) index: the same JSON repair of the Bedrock replies as the fast row (audit/patches/graphrag-3.3.0-gptoss-json-repair.py; 19,100 replies repaired). 53 of 21,727 communities (0.24%) have no report because the reply stayed invalid.

GraphRAG (standard): the index (16.6 h at 16 parallel LLM requests, about USD 102), the answers and the score were made on the operator's Linux machine (victormini1) with the same corpus slice (same corpus_sha256 as the fast index), code and scorer; the scoring environment uses the package versions of envs/pip_freeze_erag.txt. The answer latency (median 11 s, 8 parallel workers) is much lower than the fast row because the graph has fewer relationships.

systems.name: GPT-OSS + RAGFlow
systems.description: RAGFlow v0.27.2 (self-hosted), naive chunking (512 tokens, DeepDOC), text-embedding-3-large; POST /api/v1/retrieval with the default chat-assistant settings (6 chunks, hybrid keyword + vector search with vector weight 0.3, similarity threshold 0.2, no reranker); the chunks in the official answer prompt; GPT-OSS-120B on Amazon Bedrock
caveats: RAGFlow: the context is the 6 chunks of the RAGFlow retrieval API, in RAGFlow rank order, each chunk as one context document in the official answer prompt; RAGFlow's own chat prompt is not used. The document IDs are the documents of these chunks (documents.json maps the RAGFlow document IDs).

RAGFlow ingestion: RAGFlow ran in Docker (WSL2) on a separate Windows PC; the Mac sent the searches over the local network. The time (upload 281 s + parse 8,385 s) depends on the CPU of that PC. The cost is only the embedding tokens that RAGFlow counted. setup.json on the Mac was restored from the step log of the setup run (same values), and documents.json was read again from the server.

systems.name: GPT-OSS, no RAG
systems.description: GPT-OSS-120B on Amazon Bedrock with the official answer prompt and an empty Context Documents section (world-knowledge baseline)
caveats: No RAG: the official prompt says to answer only from the documents, and the document section is empty. The company is synthetic, so world knowledge cannot answer most questions.
Pilot: 50 of 500 questions, stratified by question type (2 to 17 per type). The judge (gpt-5.4) is not fully repeatable. Do not rank systems from this table.

Corpus slice: 10,000 of 511,958 documents (the 74 gold documents of the pilot questions plus 9,926 random others). Retrieval is easier than on the full corpus, so these scores are not comparable with the public leaderboard.

Official default settings: a retrieved document that is not gold can become gold for that system when 3 judges agree (correction). Recall and invalid extra documents then use a different gold list for each system. The corrected-question count is in the table.

The official scorer skips a question with no answer and no documents; that question is not in the official averages. The column 'Overall, missing = 0' counts such a question as 0 over all pilot questions.
GPT-OSS-120B on Amazon Bedrock: temperature 0.3, 4,096 max tokens, reasoning effort medium (the 4Minds server defaults), for every system except 4Minds, which uses its own GPT-OSS-120B deployment.
